commitResults.messageTitle: Add home folder resolution for app files
commitResults.messageBody:
App file locations depend on the launch directory, so launching
the JAR elsewhere can select different records.

Add HomeFolder and tests as the foundation for resolving app files
against the JAR's folder. Preserve working-directory behavior for
development runs and avoid a logging initialization dependency.

commitResults.messageTitle: Move logs to the home folder
commitResults.messageBody:
Logs follow the launch directory, separating them from the JAR.

Resolve logs against the home folder and escape percent signs so
folder names remain literal. Use the initialized base logger when
file logging fails, allowing startup to continue.

commitResults.messageTitle: Resolve preferences and data from home folder
commitResults.messageBody:
Preferences and data paths depend on the launch folder, so launching
the same JAR elsewhere can load different records.

Resolve both paths against HomeFolder and display the supplied data
path directly so file storage and the status bar use the JAR's home.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document home folder paths and launch checks
commitResults.messageBody:
The developer docs omit home folder resolution and describe logging
without its location or console fallback behavior. Testers need these
details to verify launches from another folder.

Document data, preferences, and log file locations, and add a manual
check for launching the same JAR from another folder.

Attendance date parsing accepts future dates. Attendance commands
need a separate check without restricting stats or participation.

Add an optional past-or-present date helper and fixed-date tests.
Keep existing date helpers unchanged for their other callers.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject future dates in attendance parsing
commitResults.messageBody:
Attendance parsing accepts future dates for marking and unmarking,
allowing records outside the intended date range.

Reject those dates while preserving stats, participation and loading
behavior. Use a fixed date in boundary tests for repeatable results.

Attendance rejects future dates, but the guides omit this
restriction and the limitation on removing saved future records.

Update the UG rules, DG behavior, use case, and manual checks
to describe the accepted behavior and its limitation.
